observation.visible_scene: A close, eye-level shot of two stemmed wine glasses standing side by side on a patterned (snowman/holly) tablecloth, set against a dark, heavily blurred Christmas tree with strings of small white lights and larger colored bokeh bulbs. The left glass holds a cloudy pale-yellow drink topped by a thick white foam head; the right glass holds a clearer, sparkling drink with a thinner foam head. A wooden tree ornament, a silver ball, and a small blue-and-white bauble hang in the background. Throughout the clip the glasses, tablecloth, and background ornaments stay fixed in the frame (no camera pan/zoom evident).
visible_changes: The colored background lights cycle/twinkle through blue-purple, red-pink, and green states (e.g., green dominant early, red/purple mid-clip, green returning, then purple/red again), so the overall color cast of the scene shifts over time.

Reflections and refractions on the glass rims and in the liquid change color in step with the background lights (green highlights appear on the right glass rim around t=0.47–0.53 and t=1.27–1.47, purple tints the left glass around t=0.67–0.87, etc.) — these are light reflections, not separate objects.
The foam heads in both glasses appear to slowly thin/settle: the white foam band in the left glass and especially in the right glass looks marginally lower/narrower near the end than at the start.
Small bubbles are visible within the right glass's liquid (sparkling), consistent with an ongoing fizz, though individual bubble motion is hard to track frame-by-frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the foam continues to collapse or the drinks are still being poured/settled (no pouring or contact event is seen inside the segment).
The full color sequence of the lights before t=0 and after t=2.67s.
Whether any camera motion occurs outside this static-looking excerpt.
uncertain_details: The exact rate and significance of foam settling is subtle and may partly be lighting/compression artifact.
Per-frame bubble trajectories in the right glass cannot be reliably followed.
Camera is treated as static because the glasses and background ornaments hold constant pixel positions, but this is inferred from limited background detail.

trace.prompt:
Observe this actual video clip before reading any existing caption.
These are chronological samples of a TEMPORALLY CROPPED SEGMENT of a longer source video.
Both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries, not the beginning and completion of an action. Motion
may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
Return JSON {"visible_scene":"...", "visible_changes":["observation supported within the excerpt"],
"outside_clip_unknowns":["unseen prerequisites or outcomes, only when relevant"],
"uncertain_details":["..."]}. Be concrete and concise, in English. This is not a complete event reconstruction.
